name: American Kickboxing Academy (AKA)
who: Wrestling-and-striking MMA gym in San Jose, co-founded by Javier Mendez.
why: Produced multiple UFC champions (Cain Velasquez, Daniel Cormier) and hosted Khabib Nurmagomedov's fight camps.

name: American Top Team
who: Large MMA super-team headquarters with dozens of pro fighters training under one roof.
why: Produced numerous UFC and Bellator champions since 2001; a repeat MMA Gym of the Year winner.

name: Kill Cliff FC
who: South Florida MMA team, formerly the Blackzilians, Hard Knocks 365, and Sanford MMA.
why: Home to UFC standouts Michael Chandler, Gilbert Burns, and Robbie Lawler after several rebrands.
warning: Renamed several times (Blackzilians, Hard Knocks 365, Sanford MMA, then Kill Cliff FC in 2022).

name: Tiger Muay Thai & MMA Training Camp
who: Large international training camp offering Muay Thai, MMA, and BJJ to thousands of visiting fighters yearly.
why: A global bucket-list combat-sports destination, with a training population and social reach far beyond any single team.

name: Jackson Wink MMA Academy
who: MMA academy co-founded by coaches Greg Jackson and Mike Winkeljohn.
why: Trained Jon Jones and Holly Holm among many champions; a pilgrimage stop for serious strikers and grapplers.

name: Renzo Gracie Academy
who: Historic Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu and MMA academy in Manhattan founded by Renzo Gracie.
why: One of the founding academies of the US BJJ and MMA boom; produced champions in both grappling and the cage.

name: Alliance Jiu-Jitsu San Diego
who: San Diego branch of Alliance Jiu-Jitsu, one of the most decorated BJJ organizations in the world.
why: Alliance has won more IBJJF World titles than any other team, and the San Diego room trains competitive black belts.

name: Art of Jiu-Jitsu (AOJ)
who: Competition-focused BJJ academy founded by Rafael and Guilherme Mendes.
why: Produces a steady stream of IBJJF and ADCC world champions and draws competitive grapplers worldwide.

name: B-Team Jiu-Jitsu
who: Austin no-gi grappling team founded in 2021 by former members of the Danaher Death Squad.
why: Built a large online following around elite no-gi grappling and continues to produce top ADCC competitors.
warning: Founding roster has shifted since 2021 as some members split off to form separate teams.

name: Straight Blast Gym Ireland
who: Dublin MMA academy led by coach John Kavanagh, hub of the SBG international affiliate network.
why: Developed Conor McGregor from teenager to two-division UFC champion, making it a global MMA pilgrimage site.

name: Mike's Gym
who: Dutch kickboxing gym near Amsterdam led by trainer Michael "Big Mike" Passenier.
why: Produced Glory kickboxing champions such as Murthel Groenhart and Joerie Mes, a hub of Dutch kickboxing.

name: Evolve MMA
who: Asia's largest MMA academy network, headquartered in Singapore across multiple branded locations.
why: Trained numerous ONE Championship world champions; the default combat-sports stop for visitors to Southeast Asia.

name: Wild Card Boxing Club
who: Small, famously no-frills second-floor boxing gym in Hollywood run by trainer Freddie Roach.
why: Trained Manny Pacquiao to multiple world titles; open 365 days a year and a bucket-list stop for boxing fans.

name: Gleason's Gym
who: The oldest active boxing gym in the United States, operating in Brooklyn since 1937.
why: Trained generations of world champions from the Ali era to modern pros; a living museum of boxing history.

name: Mayweather Boxing Club
who: Floyd Mayweather's private boxing gym and training center in Las Vegas.
why: Where the undefeated five-division champion trained and still mentors fighters; a stop for boxing tourists in Vegas.

name: EXOS
who: Human-performance training campus in Phoenix, headquarters of the EXOS athletic performance company.
why: Trains NFL Combine prospects and pro athletes across major leagues with sports-science-driven programs.

name: IMG Academy
who: Multi-sport boarding-school and training campus in Bradenton, Florida, covering a dozen sports.
why: World-unique in scale and facilities; alumni include top tennis, golf, and football pros across five decades.
reach: IG following split across sport-specific accounts (approx 2026, not independently confirmed)

name: Kings MMA
who: Huntington Beach MMA gym led by striking coach Rafael Cordeiro.
why: Carries the Chute Boxe striking lineage and has coached Fedor Emelianenko, Anderson Silva, and other elite strikers.

name: Fairtex Training Center
who: One of Thailand's oldest and most famous Muay Thai training camps.
why: Produced generations of Lumpinee and Rajadamnern Stadium champions; a top pilgrimage stop for Muay Thai.

name: Team Alpha Male
who: Sacramento MMA team founded in 2004 by former UFC champion Urijah Faber.
why: Produced three UFC champions (T.J. Dillashaw, Cody Garbrandt, Deiveson Figueiredo) out of one training room.

name: Xtreme Couture MMA
who: Las Vegas MMA gym founded by UFC Hall of Famer Randy Couture, now run by his son Ryan Couture.
why: Historic UFC pedigree from the Couture era continues under family ownership, with an open floor for visitors.

name: P3 Applied Sports Science
who: Sports-science and athletic-performance lab in Santa Barbara using force plates and 3D motion capture.
why: Trusted by a majority of NBA teams and the default stop for pre-draft prospects preparing for the combine.

name: Roufusport MMA Academy
who: Milwaukee-area MMA academy led by striking coach Duke Roufus.
why: Produced UFC and Bellator champions Anthony Pettis and Ben Askren under Roufus's striking system.
